claims.claim_text: Large language model systems often hallucinate false outputs and unsubstantiated answers.
claims.evidence_span: Large language model (LLM) systems, such as ChatGPT1.) or Gemini2.), can show impressive reasoning and question-answering capabilities but often ‘hallucinate’ false outputs and unsubstantiated answers3.), 4 4035–4045 (Association for Computational Linguistics, 2018).

claims.claim_text: Researchers need a general method for detecting hallucinations in LLMs that works with new and unseen questions.
claims.evidence_span: Researchers need a general method for detecting hallucinations in LLMs that works even with new and unseen questions to which humans might not know the answer.

claims.claim_text: Entropy-based uncertainty estimators can be proposed for LLMs to detect a subset of hallucinations called confabulations.
claims.evidence_span: Here we develop new methods grounded in statistics, proposing entropy-based uncertainty estimators for LLMs to detect a subset of hallucinations—confabulations—which are arbitrary and incorrect generations.

claims.claim_text: Hallucinations are defined as LLMs generating content that is nonsensical or unfaithful to the provided source content.
claims.evidence_span: Hallucinations are often defined as LLMs generating “content that is nonsensical or unfaithful to the provided source content”9.), 10 1906–1919 (Association for Computational Linguistics, 2020).
